storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com and BBA are completely different subjects.
storySpine.studentSituation: Choosing between B.Com and BBA based on title alone.
storySpine.observation: Both Joy University programmes list 'Business Organization & Management' in Semester I.
storySpine.focus: Degree title separation vs. curriculum content overlap.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If a core subject appears in both, the title alone doesn't explain the full course experience.
storySpine.changedAction: Shift focus from general degree titles to comparing specific syllabus documents.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Student marks the shared subject on a checklist and writes 'What is the rest of the syllabus?' instead of choosing a degree.
storySpine.channelExperience: Viewer sees two official PDF covers side-by-side, then zooms in on the identical Semester I row, triggering a realization that titles mask deeper content details.

candidates.title: B.Com vs BBA: The Title Myth
candidates.audienceGap: Believing degree titles dictate entire subject content.
candidates.viewerChange: Moves from title-based assumptions to evidence-based inquiry.
candidates.payoff: A more grounded method for researching courses.
candidates.support: Official Joy University syllabus documents for Semester I, page 5 and page 9 respectively.
methodSteps: Present B.Com and BBA program covers.
Highlight the shared 'Business Organization & Management' row.
Demonstrate the limitation of relying on titles alone.
Propose checking full syllabi for deeper distinction.
candidates.interpretationRule: Shared titles do not imply identical degree depth or outcomes.
candidates.visibleProof: Comparison of identical course rows in official documents.
candidates.limitations: Only applies to the inspected Semester I row; does not generalise to other years or institutions.

demonstration.input: Looking at B.Com and BBA covers.
demonstration.observation: The same subject appears in both degrees.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What else is different beyond the title?

storySpine.startingBelief: A degree decision is made by picking the 'best' title.
storySpine.studentSituation: Struggling to decide between B.Com and BBA based on online reputation.
storySpine.observation: The student has a list of 'pros' for both degrees that are equally vague.
storySpine.focus: Differentiating between general label and specific course requirements.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: Without knowing assessment criteria, the 'pro' is just a label.
storySpine.changedAction: Replaces vague 'pros' with a concrete request for specific course tasks.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Student crosses out 'Good for Jobs' and writes 'What are the Semester I core assessments?'
storySpine.channelExperience: Viewer watches a frantic 'pros/cons' list being actively dismantled and replaced by a structured, evidence-seeking question sheet.

candidates.title: Stop Guessing, Start Asking
candidates.audienceGap: Relying on vague reputational labels for degree choices.
candidates.viewerChange: From passive label-gathering to active information-gathering.
candidates.hlni: A degree decision requires knowing specific assessment requirements rather than general title prestige.
candidates.support: Logical framework of separating task, criterion, and feedback.
methodSteps: List current unknown factors for each programme.
Formulate specific questions for admissions or course briefs.
Refine the search to seek actual criteria.
candidates.interpretationRule: Vague labels are not evidence; specific assessment tasks are the only reliable data.
candidates.visibleProof: A three-column grid showing Task, Criterion, and Feedback.
candidates.limitations: Requires access to course briefs; will not provide a 'correct' degree choice.

demonstration.input: List of pros for B.Com and BBA.

issues: trust-syllabus-001 | payoff: The visible consequence consists only of a student writing a generic research question. A research question that does not visibly improve the student's next step or act as a concrete correction to the starting belief is insufficient as a payoff. Correction: The student replaces their initial degree choice list with a comparative table identifying shared and distinct modules found in both programme PDFs, demonstrating a move from title-based assumption to evidence-based content comparison.

issues: trust-syllabus-v2 | payoff: The visible consequence is a research instruction rather than a concrete use of the insight to improve a decision. A restatement of the need for information ('What is the rest of the syllabus?') is not a completed action that demonstrates the consequence of the insight on the student's next step.
